A.truth: false as an unconditional claim; no contextual condition can make habitual unassessed checks guarantee optimal coverage of any product
A.wrong_model: Experience and routine alone automatically optimize coverage universally
A.concrete_problem: Universal optimum and risk-blindness are untenable; a plausible distractor with coherent reasoning.

B.wrong_model: Strategy is a one-time immutable decision whose purpose is to prevent adaptation
B.concrete_problem: Contradicts risk/goal changes; coherent as a wrong model.

C.truth: false; confuses strategy with retrospective report
C.wrong_model: Strategy records only completed tests and does not guide future priorities
C.concrete_problem: Explicitly answers both parts, though as a coherent misconception.

D.truth: defensible and consistent with contextual risk-based approach

Q1.CONTENT: Pass for visible stem/options: each option defines a strategy and states why it exists; wrong options are sufficiently complete false models, not fragments. D's response is aligned to both halves.
Q1.FACTS: No special quantitative/standard claim in option text. Risk, constraints, quality goals, and useful feedback are defensible contextual elements.
Q1.LINKAGE: All four options use the same definition+purpose axis. A-C actively answer rather than evade.
Q1.SECTIONS: All 17 supplied sections accounted for (A-D: 4+4+4+5). Wrong sections generally explain the relevant misconception. Counterfactuals follow from the option's premise; no clear hidden condition needed. D's five sections support the option without being used to cure option incompleteness.

SFPL.finding: No longest-correct signal: A is 2 chars longer than D. Similar overall lengths; no conspicuous format/grammar cue observed.

Q1.ANSC: Pass: A-D each address both definition and purpose; none is a single-term answer or adjacent fact.
Q1.RU: Clear and natural overall. 'Автоматически получать оптимальное покрытие любого продукта' is deliberately overclaiming but intelligible; no linguistic ambiguity that rescues A.

A.wrong_model: A fixed numerical quota defines and governs application regardless of product
A.concrete_problem: Universal ratio is an overclaim, but the option clearly supplies a full mistaken model and prescription.

B.truth: defensible as a common version; qualifies proportions by risk and feedback cost
B.concrete_problem: No substantive content defect. 'быстрые узкие unit' is a common tendency rather than an invariant; the next clause explicitly says proportions depend on context.

C.truth: false: reverses the conventional pyramid and proposes broad UI paths for most logic branches
C.wrong_model: Broad E2E tests form the base and carry detailed branch coverage
C.concrete_problem: Clear inverted model plus use; wrong but sufficiently complete.

D.truth: false as a universal rule; architecture label alone does not justify reducing integration checks
D.wrong_model: Microservices always warrant fewer integration tests regardless of interaction risk
D.concrete_problem: The first clause is a conventional layer listing; second supplies an erroneous unconditional application. Complete answer to both requested parts.

Q2.CONTENT: Pass for visible stem/options: each option names a model and gives an application rule. A, C, and D are coherent false models; B gives a qualified common model.
Q2.FACTS: The ratio 70/20/10 is correctly rejected as non-universal. No fixed durations are stated in options. Risk-dependent allocation is sound. D's mandatory reduction is indefensible without a further condition; its wording explicitly excludes risk dependence.
Q2.LINKAGE: All options address both model and application. They stay on layer/granularity/allocation rather than changing to a neighboring concept.
Q2.SECTIONS: All 17 sections accounted for (A-D: 4+5+4+4). Wrong-model explanations and counterfactuals are generally coherent. C's counterfactual correctly describes the inverted distribution. D's counterfactual follows from its unconditional rule. No relevant sections omitted.

SFPL.finding: Key B is longest by one character over C, but C is nearly identical in length and has more words (21 vs 24 for B? actual split counts: B 24, C 21); textual complexity may offer a mild surface cue, but no decisive longest-only signal. Other options use same single-sentence definition/application structure.

Q2.ANSC: Pass: all four options answer both the model and application halves; D's erroneous rule still provides an explicit application, not an omission.
Q2.RU: Clear and idiomatic enough. 'по норме 70/20/10' and 'долю ... сокращают' are unambiguous overclaims intentionally used as wrong models.

A.concrete_problem: No substantive content defect. A concise list of content categories is sufficient for this broad stem.

B.truth: false: describes a possible test report and excludes the strategy function
B.wrong_model: Strategy document is exclusively retrospective execution reporting
B.concrete_problem: Coherent confusion between report and strategy; fully answers by asserting contents and exclusion.

C.truth: false: substitutes test-case catalogue for strategic approach
C.wrong_model: A catalogue of detailed scenarios alone constitutes strategy; goals/risks/selection rationale are outside it
C.concrete_problem: Plausible category confusion and a full false account, not a fragment.

D.truth: false: schedule alone does not establish a testing strategy
D.wrong_model: Strategy document is exclusively calendar/assignment planning
D.concrete_problem: Plausible confusion with planning; explicitly addresses its content and purpose.

Q5.CONTENT: Pass for visible stem/options: A defines the document and names representative contents. B-D each assert a complete alternative document model. It is not necessary for A to enumerate every possible section given context-dependent form.
Q5.FACTS: The stated relation to test plans is appropriately qualified. ISTQB CTFL 4.0.1 §5.1.1 (syllabus printed p.48) says the test plan describes objectives, resources and processes; includes test approach; and demonstrates adherence to existing policy/strategy or explains deviation. Thus no universal organization-versus-release boundary is asserted. The ten theory items are explicitly a practical menu, not an official mandatory checklist.
Q5.LINKAGE: All options answer what the document is and what it contains; B-D use plausible neighboring artifacts as complete distractor models.
Q5.SECTIONS: All 17 sections accounted for (A-D: 5+4+4+4). Sections explain the specific wrong model. Counterfactuals are generally logical and do not depend on invented context. A's edge case accurately avoids rigid strategy/plan separation.

SFPL.finding: Correct A is not longest; wrong D is longest (167 chars). All options use a similar one-sentence form.

Q5.ANSC: Pass: each option addresses definition and contents; A includes examples of contents and is sufficient for the breadth of the stem.
Q5.RU: Natural and readable. English artifact names are established technical terms; the Russian explanatory wording is clear. No grammar or phrasing gives away A.

topics.Q1: Definition and rationale are coherent, contextual and practical. Risks, scope, resources, exit criteria and feedback are presented as related choices, not guarantees. The sample diagram's path from exit criteria through quality gates to release decision is a useful conceptual relationship, not a universal decision rule; surrounding prose qualifies it as context-dependent.
topics.Q2: Model description matches ISTQB CTFL 4.0.1 §5.1.6 and Cohn's original three-layer model. CTFL explicitly permits differing layer count/names and says higher layers have lower granularity/isolation and longer execution; prose correctly treats speed/cost as tendencies depending on implementation/environment. The staged YAML is explicitly an illustrative stage outline, not executable pipeline or mandated ordering; prose says real jobs, dependencies, parallelism and gates vary. No fixed 70/20/10, time bands, or microservices integration share is claimed. Minor presentation caveat: the stage list visually presents a linear ordering, but the adjacent disclaimer directly neutralizes that interpretation.
topics.Q5: The ten content headings are clearly labeled a practical discussion list, not a required standard/template. Document scope and format are contextualized. Strategy/test-plan relationship is accurate and appropriately qualified against ISTQB §5.1.1; no blanket organization-vs-release distinction is made. Maintenance guidance is sensible practice, not represented as a normative standard.

theory.overall: No material theory-level factual or logical defect found in assigned topics. Practical examples and diagrams are identified/contextualized rather than overstated. Russian is understandable and largely natural; technical English labels are consistent.

primary_sources.read: §5.1.1, printed p.48 (test plan purpose/content); §5.1.6, printed pp.50-51 (pyramid granularity, isolation, duration, variable layer names); browser-opened official PDF lines matched those sections.
primary_sources.verified_claims: Test plan describes objectives/resources/processes, includes test approach, and documents adherence to existing strategy or explains deviation. Pyramid supports automation/effort allocation; lower tests are small/isolated/fast, top E2E broader/slower; layer number/names can vary; original Cohn model is unit/service/UI.
